structured.species.shortDescription: Naturally evolved, furred humanoids whose rabbit-like skull, face, long ears, and powerful jumping anatomy are convergent traits rather than evidence of rabbit ancestry.
structured.species.classification: Natural sapient humanoid Species; exact formal taxonomy not yet authored
structured.species.biologySummary: Two-armed, two-legged, plantigrade, furred humanoids with two long auditory/sensory ears, broad ordinary genetic variation in adult frame, specialized spring-leg anatomy, oxygen-breathing endothermic omnivory, approximately 25% faster metabolism than the human comparison baseline, and a voluntary coordinated peak-output capability known as Burst.
structured.species.appearanceSummary: Rabbit-like skull, nose, face, and long expressive ears; five digits per hand and foot; large plantigrade feet; thick nail-like claws; no tail; human-like external hand arrangement and teeth; wide natural coat colors and patterns; head hair, manes, crests, and thicker fur patches can occur. Vivid unnatural coat colors are cosmetic.
structured.species.typicalSize: Central approximately 50%: 4 ft 9 in–6 ft 2 in and 90–250 lb
structured.species.cultureSummary: Akwi cultures are intentionally diverse. Twiloni and Azerkiji are established examples; neither culture nor the broader Akavic identity is inherited biology.
structured.species.societySummary: Akwi societies vary across a’Wiio and the diaspora. Readiness-based adulthood and a widespread but uneven protective-duty tradition are established social institutions, not biological traits.
structured.species.senses: Ordinary human-comparable channels plus approximately 20% stronger attentive hearing and ear-based magnetoreception, pressure, airflow, tactile, and positional information; no established dimensional-instability sense
structured.species.locomotion: Normal upright walking plus exceptional vertical and horizontal jumping; swimming, climbing, and burrowing broadly comparable to the supplied human baseline
structured.species.biologicalLimitations: Lower sustained-exertion profile than the human marathon comparison; Burst produces recovery demand and overuse risk; long ears require equipment accommodation and are exposed sensory structures; hearing requires attention for useful benefit.
structured.species.languageSummary: Twil is the major travel lingua franca; Kitell is another major a’Wiio language. Many other languages exist. Species selection alone should not yet imply a language grant.

species.ownerApprovedMagneticOrientation.homeworldExperience: a’Wiio’s shifting magnetic field is experienced more like a moving ocean and does not naturally provide a stable compass direction.

species.ownerApprovedHearing.relativeAttentiveStrength: approximately 20% stronger than the supplied human comparison baseline

species.ownerApprovedJumping.biologicalReference: Standing vertical jump around two to three times the Akwi’s height at a’Wiio-equivalent gravity without meaningful burden.
